topic.title: How deep the Channel Tunnel runs under the sea between England and France: two rail tunnels and a service tunnel in chalk, an undersea crossover cavern, and the lowest point below the waves

title: The Channel Tunnel: How Deep Do the Trains Go?
description:
The Channel Tunnel takes trains from England to France under the sea. How far down is it?
Sources: Getlink, Wikipedia (2025).
Depths from published sources. Cutaway illustrations, not to scale.
cta: Under the sea or under a mountain: which tunnel should we dive next? Comment

lines.text: A train to Paris dives under the sea in the Channel Tunnel. How far down?
Below the seabed, it races through soft chalk.
Between its rail tunnels runs a smaller one, for repairs and rescues.
Under the sea, a huge cavern lets trains swap tunnels. How deep now?
On average, it runs 40 m below the seabed.
And 37.9 km of the tunnel runs under the sea.
Then the train climbs back out, into France.

Crossover caverns under the sea (Getlink: 7 km off England, 13 km off France), service tunnel for maintenance and rescue (Getlink), and chalk all match. [script] 15.0-17.3 s, beat 'deep' (the turn): the 40 m figure is spoken at ~15.8 s but its 'BELOW SEABED' tablet only starts on 'below' (~16.3 s), still reads 20 m at 16.5 s, reaches 40 m at ~17.07 s and is replaced by 'UNDER THE SEA' at ~17.3 s: the turn's figure is readable for about 0.2 s and only after it was said, so on mute the 40 m is effectively never seen. Put the tally on 'average' or 'runs' (tallies[0].on) so it lands before the figure is spoken and holds for the rest of the beat.

[script] 15.0-21.0 s, beats 'deep' and 'length': two beats in a row are the same picture (the DEEP CHALK tunnel with the same white/yellow train, only the tablet text changes), and that tunnel is also the same picture as 'rail' at 4.5-6.0 s. Start the pull-back on 'And'/'tunnel' so the payoff beat is its own wide picture of the whole crossing under the sea.

[script] 21.0 s (end of the payoff beat 'length', on 'sea.'): the new pull-back lands on a frame that is about 80% flat grey chalk. The four tunnels are tiny boxes about 210 px wide stacked in the middle, their signs and the 37.9 km tablet are gone, and the sea is a thin strip cut off at the top edge. The payoff ends emptier than any other still and doesn't show the undersea run. The gap comes from the layers' depths: rail ft 230, service 290, cavern 360, deep 430, under a seabed at about 20 ft, so the stack is mostly empty chalk above them. Bring the tunnels up close under the seabed (e.g. 60/90/120/160 ft; the depths are 'none', so no figure changes), or end the pull tighter, so the whole crossing with the sea fills the frame and stays readable.
